Who logged in? What role were they assigned? Was MFA used? The Inherited Identity Risk Gap Agent-AI expands exposure Who owns this agent or service account? Identity security used to focus on who can log in. The next challenge is controlling what identities execute. jobs.title: About Us
jobs.description: Bringing Clarity to the Complexity of Identity The Platform Use Cases Use Cases Identity & Access Management Programs Incident Response Teams GRC & Audit M&A / Growth Events Guardrails for Autonomous Identity Customers Company Company About Us Careers Resources Resources Resources All Blog Events & Webinars Reports & Papers News Guides Partner Sign In Partner Sign In Book a demo Orchid Exists Because Identity Lost Its Center Identity security used to feel centralized. Today, it lives across IAM, applications, infrastructure, and code. Orchid was built to bring coherence back to that sprawl. Download Our Solution Brief Our Vision Identity security no longer lives in one system It spans IAM, applications, infrastructure, and code - each enforcing access in different ways, with no shared source of truth. Orchid’s vision is to make this fragmented identity behavior observable and explainable end to end. So identity teams can understand how access actually works, bring applications under governance, and prove control over time - without relying on assumptions or manual effort Our Story While entrepreneur-in-residence at Team8, one of Israel’s most successful VC funds, Roy Katmor was tasked with exploring emerging theses in the security space. One, in particular, stood out and sparked his quest - the challenge of onboarding applications and adopting the latest identity security controls. Leveraging its extensive CISO network and over the course of three years, Team8 identified a top-three enterprise concern, a top-three budget investment, and most surprisingly, a top-three source of dissatisfaction all related to identity consumption. The issue appeared to stem from enterprises struggling to integrate and maintain applications within their identity stack, resulting in failure to meet regulatory and security policies within the fragmented identity space. Yet, just one year later, after extensive research into emerging technologies — primarily LLMs that were not available a few years prior — the team, now joined by Robert Wiseman and Ido Kelson, discovered that utilizing LLMs to interpret application instructions can reveal identity-related context and reasoning in each application’s design, providing the missing piece needed to address the complexity of identity and access management. With this breakthrough, and a lot of hard work, they succeeded in developing a ground-breaking Identity-first Security Orchestration solution that discovers all applications in use throughout an enterprise, assesses their identity flows to highlight exposure, and enables the remediation of that exposure to strengthen and maintain the organization’s identity security posture. Who We Are Orchid is led by a team of seasoned executives with a proven track record of successful entrepreneurship, deep AI and cybersecurity expertise, and demonstrated product-market-fit and go-to-market strategies within the security industry. Roy Katmor Co-Founder & CEO Roy Katmor Co-Founder & CEO Roy Katmor is an experienced executive with a strong entrepreneurial background, blending deep technical expertise with a proven track record in product-market fit and go-to-market strategies within the security industry. In his previous role, Roy was the GM and VP of Endpoint Security at Fortinet (NASDAQ: FTNT), following the successful acquisition of enSilo, a real-time automated endpoint security company backed by LightSpeed Ventures, which he founded and led as CEO for over five years. Before enSilo, Roy held various product strategy, management, and R&D leadership roles at both public and private companies, including Akamai, Imperva, Trustwave, and SAP. Robert Wiseman Co-Founder, GM and VP R&D Robert Wiseman Co-Founder, GM and VP R&D Robert leads both the technical and business operations, including all aspects of customer success. Previously, as VP at Team8 Enterprise Foundry, Robert led the incubation of cybersecurity startups, guiding them from ideation to growth. He played a key role in refining ideas, securing early customer engagements, and advising founders on strategy. Since 2021, Robert has also served as a Board Observer for Gem Security (acquired by Wiz) and OX.Security. Prior to Team8, Robert held leadership roles in research and presales at Claroty, an IoT security unicorn, and served as VP of Technical Operations at Bionic (acquired by Crowdstrike). Ido Kelson Co-Founder and Chief Software Architect Ido Kelson Co-Founder and Chief Software Architect Throughout his career, Ido has led engineering teams as well as spearheaded, designed and developed patented technology across different cybersecurity domains. Before co-founding Orchid, Ido was chief architect of endpoint solution at Fortinet (NASDAQ: FTNT), following the successful acquisition of enSilo, an award-winning real-time automated endpoint security company, which he co-founded and served as its VP of Engineering. Prior to enSilo, Ido led various R&D teams, designing and building Imperva's core platform, as a key member of the company from its initial startup stage and through to its positioning as a public global leading cybersecurity company. Tal Herman CPO Tal Herman CPO Tal Herman is a leader in Identity and Access Management (IAM) and is currently Chief Product Officer at Orchid. Previously VP of Product Management at Okta, Tal built Okta Identity Governance from the ground up into a thriving business, laid the foundation for Okta Privileged Access, and drove innovation across products like Universal Directory and Secure Partner Access. With over 20 years of experience, including leadership roles at CA Technologies, ForgeRock, and OneLogin, she focused on delivering transformative solutions, securing identity data for millions, and shaping the future of identity security.
